bio: Works a desk job in marketing, cooks most dinners, wants more energy for weekend hikes.
dayToDay: desk job 9 to 5:30. i usually skip breakfast and just have an iced latte, lunch is whatever's near the office, i cook dinner most nights. i snack a lot around 4pm when i'm tired
exercise: walk the dog every morning, like 30 min. pilates tuesday and thursday evenings. hike on weekends when the weather's ok
goodPlan: A loss range below her maintenance and at or above 1,200; ties the 4pm snacking and the skipped breakfast to her logged days; protein nudged up from ~80-100 g; keeps the walks and pilates; relaxed, realistic pace for June.

dayToDay: i'm a nurse, three 12 hour night shifts a week (usually sun mon tue, 7pm to 7am). on shift i graze on whatever's in the break room, vending machine stuff around 3am. i sleep 8am to 2pm after shifts. on my days off i try to flip back to normal and end up eating at weird times
exercise: honestly not much, i'm on my feet all shift. i want to get to the gym 2x a week on days off

sessions.notes: first time back in a while

goodPlan: Built around the shift pattern (a pre-shift meal and a planned 3am snack instead of vending), a range that holds on shift days, protein raised from ~65 g, two realistic gym days; honest that the trend is slow so far.

timeframe: 3 weeks, it's for my sister's wedding
dayToDay: i've been doing around 900 calories a day to speed things up. black coffee until 2pm, then a salad, small dinner. i'm kind of exhausted and cold all the time but it's working i think
exercise: spin class 5 mornings a week at 6am
goodPlan: Sets a range at or above her 1,200 floor and explains warmly why eating MORE will make her look and feel better at the wedding (energy for spin, muscle kept, less water and fatigue); honest that 3 weeks is short and gives the realistic version; no shaming, no refusal.

dayToDay: work from home so my schedule is flexible. i eat pretty clean during the week, a lot of eggs, salads and chicken. i have a sweet tooth after dinner
exercise: just started couch to 5k, 3 runs a week
goodPlan: Says plainly that 30 lb in 6 weeks is not realistic and gives the realistic version (a pace and a date), with a range that keeps her at or above 1,200 and supports the runs; something good to aim for by July instead; still motivating.

timeframe: by the end of the year
dayToDay: vegetarian for 8 years (i eat eggs and dairy, no meat or fish). lunch is the work cafeteria, usually pasta or a veggie wrap. i don't really like protein powder
exercise: yoga 3x a week, and i bike to work, 20 min each way
goodPlan: Protein target realistic for a vegetarian who dislikes powder, with named vegetarian sources (eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, lentils, tofu, edamame) that fit the cafeteria lunch; names the ~50-65 g days; no meat or fish suggested.

dayToDay: teacher, up at 6, lunch is packed from home. i'm usually wiped after school and snack while grading
exercise: i used to run but tore my meniscus in the spring, physio says no running or jumping for now. i can swim and do upper body. the pool is open mon wed fri mornings
goodPlan: Training built only on swimming and upper body (nothing that loads the knee: no running, jumping or lunges), the after-school grading snack handled with a plan, a range below maintenance and at or above 1,200; trend so far is slow and it says so.

timeframe: ongoing, i just want to stay here
dayToDay: hit my goal last month!! now i'm scared of gaining it back. i've been eating about the same as when i was losing because i don't know how much more i can eat
exercise: lifting 3x a week (full body), long walk on sundays
goodPlan: A maintenance range (around what she burns, above her loss-phase intake) with the reassurance that eating more now keeps the result; a way to step calories up and watch the trend; celebrates hitting the goal; keeps the lifting.

dayToDay: just downloaded this. i work retail and my shifts change every week, sometimes i close until 10pm. i eat a lot of fast food on closing nights
exercise: nothing right now, i want to start walking
goodPlan: An openly early read (one weigh-in, no food logged) that does not pretend to know her intake; a starter range below maintenance and at or above 1,200; closing-night fast food handled with specific better orders; a gentle walking start; asks her to log a few days.

dayToDay: accountant, very routine during the week, i meal prep my lunches. friday and saturday nights are dinners out and drinks with friends and i don't want to give that up
exercise: gym 3x a week before work (mon wed fri), mostly machines
goodPlan: Spots that Friday and Saturday (2,500-2,900 kcal) undo the weekday deficit, which explains the flat trend; keeps the weekend social life with a concrete strategy (bank a little, protein first, drink swaps); weekly-average framing.
Works from the data alone (ten weigh-ins drifting down, one day of food) without inventing a routine she never described; an early read that hedges; a loss range at or above 1,200.

bio: Software engineer, lifts in the evenings, wants to put on muscle without getting soft.
dayToDay: office job, i meal prep chicken and rice on sundays and eat lunch at my desk. dinner after the gym around 8
exercise: push pull legs, 4 days a week (mon tue thu sat), about an hour each
goodPlan: A gain range above his maintenance that keeps the lean pace he is already on (~0.3-0.5 lb a week), protein ~140-170 g which he already hits (a win), progressive overload on the PPL split; nothing called excessive.

timeframe: i want to hit 172 by the end of next year
dayToDay: i've always been skinny. i just don't get hungry, i forget to eat lunch most days and i get full really fast. big meals make me feel sick
exercise: climbing gym 2x a week and i just started a beginner lifting program 3x a week
goodPlan: A range above his maintenance (his ~2,000 kcal days explain the flat-to-down trend), made doable for a small appetite: calorie-dense, easy foods, liquid calories, more frequent small meals, reminders for the skipped lunch; eating is framed as the work, never too much.

dayToDay: i work at a startup, 60+ hour weeks, i eat whatever i can grab, a lot of delivery. i sleep maybe 6 hours
exercise: i only have 20 minutes, 3 mornings a week, at home with dumbbells and a pull-up bar
goodPlan: A minimal-effort plan that fits 20-minute home sessions (compound dumbbell moves, pull-ups), high-protein delivery orders he can actually pick, a gain range above maintenance, a nod to sleep; nothing that needs meal prep hours he does not have.

timeframe: through the half marathon in march
dayToDay: physical therapist, on my feet a lot. i want to keep my weight steady while training, last time i trained i lost 8 lb and felt flat
exercise: half marathon plan: 4 runs a week (tue thu sat long run, sun recovery), long run is 10 to 12 miles now, plus one lifting session
goodPlan: A maintenance range that rises with long-run days (fuel around the runs), so he does not repeat the 8 lb loss; carbs framed as fuel; protein for recovery; holds steady as the goal; no deficit.

dayToDay: been on a dirty bulk, eating everything. pizza, burgers, a gallon of milk a week. my waist is getting bigger faster than my lifts
goodPlan: Names the fast gain (the trend reads about 1.3 lb a week) and explains that a slower gain stays leaner; a range still above his maintenance but below the ~3,500-4,100 kcal he eats now; better food quality without calling eating bad; keeps the protein.
